More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. What you’ll do IntelliJ IDEA changed how Java development worked by introducing automated refactoring, and it remains a core tool for thousands of developers worldwide. We need an independent QA Engineer to help us ensure these enterprise development tools remain reliable and efficient. You will take ownership of the testing process for new and existing functionality, balancing manual exploratory testing with automated test development. You will work closely with developers to spot flaws early and collaborate directly with product managers to decide which issues impact our users most. Day to day, you will: Perform exploratory testing of new and existing features to uncover edge cases. Run regression tests to ensure platform stability before releases. Maintain, write, and scale our automated test suites. Reproduce user-reported issues and provide technical support to resolve them. Collaborate with developers to share product knowledge and diagnose system bugs. Work with product managers to estimate the priority and business impact of issues. What you’ll bring Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical problems clearly. Independence, self-discipline, and a habit of learning new technologies on your own. A collaborative approach to working with distributed engineering teams. What you’ll need Proven experience testing commercial software applications. Proficiency in Java or Kotlin sufficient to write test applications and read source code. Fluency in spoken and written English. Practical familiarity with build tools (like Maven, Gradle, or Bazel), databases, and Docker containers. Experience testing software across different operating systems alongside basic system administration skills. What success looks like Success in this role means earning the trust of your team through sound testing decisions and leaving our codebase cleaner and more stable than you found it. You will move past simple task lists to take real ownership of product quality, helping the team ship reliable updates without compromising speed. Ultimately, success is defined by preventing regressions and ensuring enterprise developers have a seamless experience using our tools. Why join JetBrains? Strong base salary. We offer competitive pay that reflects your skills and experience. Flexible work location. Enjoy the freedom to work from home or from the office. Remote work. Spend up to 30 days per year working remotely from abroad. Extra time off. More days to relax, recharge, and do the things you love. Medical insurance allowance. Enjoy peace of mind for you and your family Learning and development opportunities. Access to conferences, courses, and language classes. Relocation support. We help make your move as smooth and stress-free as possible. Language classes. Pick up the local language or sharpen your English skills. Fuel your day. Enjoy a hot meal or receive a lunch allowance on workdays. Mental health support. To help you feel your best, we provide easy access to professional mental health services. Sports benefit. Enjoy an on-site gym or sports club stipend. Internal events. Join company-wide celebrations and team gatherings. *Some benefits may vary depending on location. Exceptional electromechanical aptitude with ability to disassemble and reassemble complex equipment with little instruction. Strong computer skills and ability to learn new software. Ability to adapt to a constantly changing environment with new technologies, equipment and processes. ~2 years of hands-on experience with electromechanical testing, troubleshooting and failure analysis.Additional Preferred Skills Basic familiarity with German Standards for Electronics and Electricity is a plus. By unifying complex business services under a high-performance platform umbrella, we provide a holistic API-first environment that empowers our partners to grow their business with speed and flexibility. At Forto, we are at the forefront of change, harnessing the power of AI to revolutionise logistics. We want to reinvent digital supply chains to be transparent, frictionless and sustainable. From day one, our mission has been to simplify global trade – creating a seamless and efficient logistics process. Your role & Mission The Site Reliability Engineering team at Forto is responsible for reliability and developer experience. We enable our development teams to write complex business logic by providing best-in-class tooling and infrastructure. We have a production environment based on GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, and Helm. On top of that, we have self-service tooling written in TypeScript. “You build it, you run it” – our job is to make that real. This is a high-ownership role on a lean team that directly shapes how 70+ engineers build and ship software. If you care about platform quality and want your work felt immediately across an engineering org, this is a great match for you. What you will do Build out our runtime platform as a self-service product that enables our engineering teams to write code, run workloads, and drive engineering culture forward. Bring software development skills and practices into platform engineering, such as code quality, domain-driven design, and test-driven development. Own the developer portal and internal platform roadmap, including leading this year’s overhaul of our CI/CD pipelines in collaboration with all product teams. Ensure site reliability by building observability solutions, deployment, and disaster recovery capabilities. Own reliability standards end-to-end through SLOs and error budgets — shaping how teams balance velocity and risk. Drive infrastructure cost optimisation across Kubernetes, MongoDB, and Datadog at scale. Improve our security posture through tooling, compliance work, and partnership with security stakeholders. Work closely with the entire Engineering function as a steward of platform architecture — embracing new technologies and cleaning up old ones. Improve developer productivity by working with engineers on platform services and developer tooling. Serve as a second line of defense for incidents and be the secondary on-call for our developers. Required Skills and Experience 5+ years in backend or infrastructure engineering, with at least 2 years in an SRE or platform engineering role. Hands-on experience with GCP/AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, and Helm in a production environment. Strong software development background — building frameworks, internal tooling, and infrastructure. Experience with an observability platform (Datadog or equivalent) at scale — not just dashboards, but alerting strategy, cost management, and SLO instrumentation. Experience defining and operating SLOs and error budgets as a reliability mechanism, not just as metrics. Solid understanding of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and a GitOps-first mindset. Proven track record designing, developing, and troubleshooting complex distributed systems. Don’t fit all of our criteria? That’s okay! We know that you might be hesitant to apply if you don’t meet all our requirements, but here at Forto, we pride ourselves on embracing diverse perspectives and celebrating potential. If you are passionate about this position and the Forto values, please apply anyway. There could be a place for you in this role – or another one that’s a perfect fit! Why work with us? Our team is hard-working, constantly seeking to maximise the impact of their work, but we put our people first, always winning with care. We value efficient systems and swift, direct communication. We want everyone to have their time to speak, so that we can embrace diverse perspectives to help drive towards solutions always. Imagine leading the charge in establishing self-driven laboratories that autonomously design, synthesize, test, and evaluate advanced materials. You will integrate AI-based material design with automated experimentation, creating a seamless workflow that accelerates innovation cycles. By leveraging closed-loop learning, you will continuously enhance digital material models for industrial energy applications, making a significant impact on our mission to drive sustainable energy solutions. How You’ll Make an Impact * Definition and deployment of self-driven lab architectures for streamlined materials development * Integration of AI-based material design with automated synthesis and testing for enhanced efficiency * Design of robotic and parallel experimentation workflows for rapid material innovation * Establishment of closed-loop optimization between machine learning models and lab execution for continuous improvement * Management of large volumes of experimental and sensor data ensuring FAIRness and traceability * Continuous improvement of machine learning models through experimental feedback and bridging of digital predictions with physical validation and scale-up to ensure real-world impact What You Bring * Completed PhD or Master’s degree in Materials Science, Engineering, Physics, or a related discipline * Extensive hands-on experience in R&D or engineering environments * Deep expertise in materials synthesis, characterization, and advanced testing techniques * Demonstrated experience with automation, robotics, and high-throughput experimentation * Strong foundation in AI/ML and data-driven approaches to optimization and process improvement * Extensive experience in closed-loop or self-driven lab environments, coupled with strong leadership and communication skills across technical and business domains About the Team In our Business Functions we enable our organization to reach their targets by providing best-in class services and solutions in the areas of IT, HR, Finance, Real Estate, Strategy & Technology and more. Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. You implement waveform control and signal processing algorithms bare metal on an NXP radar SoC driving our 77 GHz front end, verify them against measurements in the lab, and keep the chain inside its timing, memory, and power budget. You work directly with the Radar Systems Architect on algorithm design, with the embedded Linux team on the platform your firmware runs on, and with the perception team on the micro-Doppler data their classification models consume. Key Responsibilities Implement radar signal processing algorithms bare metal on the DSP cores of our NXP radar SoC Define and maintain the firmware architecture for the radar signal chain Implement waveform generation, timing, and control for the 77 GHz front end Verify algorithm behaviour against lab measurements, including the test setups needed to characterize it Analyze and optimize runtime, memory, and power consumption on the target hardware Produce and maintain the micro-Doppler data products the perception team's classification models are trained and run on Work with the Radar Systems Architect to bring algorithm designs onto the target Work with the embedded Linux team on interfaces, build integration, and firmware updates Required Qualifications 7+ years of hands-on firmware or DSP development for embedded signal processing systems (a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, or a related field is welcome, though equivalent practical experience counts just as much) Practical experience with radar signal processing algorithms such as detection, tracking, or clutter suppression Experience planning and running radar measurements, and comparing the results against expected algorithm behaviour Experience with bare-metal development on multicore SoCs: startup and memory layout, DMA, and interrupt latency Solid C skills, plus working proficiency in at least one of C++, Rust, or DSP assembly Experience defining firmware architecture for a shipped product, not only for prototypes Experience with software and hardware performance analysis: profiling, timing, memory, and power on the target Nice to Have Experience with FMCW radar and multi-channel or MIMO front ends Experience with fixed-point implementation and numerical accuracy analysis Experience with vendor DSP toolchains and SDKs, ideally the NXP radar SDK Practical command of laboratory instruments such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and vector network analyzers Contributions to open-source signal processing or embedded projects German language skills are beneficial but not required Arbeitsorte Karte anzeigen Hainstr. 2, 01097 Dresden Als Projektingenieur:in für Stationsleittechnik bei Schneider Electric übernimmst Du die technische Leitung anspruchsvoller Leittechnikprojekte – von Nieder- bis Hochspannung. Du betreust unsere Industrie- und Energieversorgungskunden deutschlandweit und gelegentlich international. Gemeinsam mit einem engagierten Team gestaltest Du eine nachhaltigere Zukunft durch digitale Energie- und Automatisierungslösungen. Klingt spannend? Dann bewirb Dich jetzt und werde IMPACT Maker bei Schneider Electric! Alle wichtigen Informationen für Dich auf einen Blick: Wann und wo? Ab sofort in Dresden Dauer: Unbefristet Urlaub: 30 Tage/Jahr Wochenstunden : 40 Deine Ansprechperson? Franziska Ludwig Unser Angebot: Verantwortung: Du übernimmst die technische Projektabwicklung von Leittechniklösungen in komplexen Energieanlagen – von Nieder- bis Hochspannung. Kundennähe: Du betreust Industrie- und Energieversorgungskunden deutschlandweit und gelegentlich auch international. Nachhaltigkeit: Gemeinsam mit Deinem Team gestaltest Du die Energiewelt von morgen durch digitale Automatisierungs- und Energiemanagementlösungen. Karrierechance: Werde Teil von Schneider Electric und gestalte mit uns eine nachhaltigere Zukunft – als IMPACT Maker! Dein IMPACT: Projektion: Du planst, prüfst und nimmst Geräte und Systeme der konventionellen sowie digitalen Schutz- und Schaltanlagenleittechnik in Betrieb. Mitgestaltung: Du wirkst aktiv an Pflichtenheften mit und bedienst moderne Test- und Prüfsysteme, z. B. für Kommunikationsprotokolle oder Schutzgeräte. Dein Profil: Qualifikation: Du hast eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Elektrotechniker:in oder ein Studium der Elektro- bzw. Automatisierungstechnik. Erfahrung: Du bringst erste Berufserfahrung in einem technischen Umfeld mit – idealerweise bereits mit Projektbezug. Arbeitsweise: Du arbeitest strukturiert, flexibel und zuverlässig, triffst gern Entscheidungen und findest kreative Lösungen mit einem guten Gespür für Dringlichkeit. Sprachkompetenz: Du verfügst über fließende Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse – auch für internationale Kundenkontakte. Technikverständnis (optional): Du hast Kenntnisse in Hard- und Software sowie in der Rechner-Kommunikation. Dein nächster Schritt? Online bewerben natürlich!
